name: Context Mode
tagline: A background service that keeps large tool results out of your AI coding agent's memory, so sessions last longer and cost less.
sentence: Install it once and your AI coding sessions run for hours instead of hitting memory limits after 30 minutes - a 315 KB test result becomes a 5.4 KB summary the agent can still search.

visual.alt: A YouTube thumbnail in pixel art style: a pink brain illustration on the left with '99% SAVINGS' in bold white text above it and a curved arrow pointing down, with 'CLAUDE CODE' in orange pixel-style lettering on the right, all on a dark background.
visual.caption: The project's demo video thumbnail, claiming 99% savings on Claude Code context usage.

board.say: Your AI coding agent's conversation fills up fast. Every test output, log file, and code search it reads eats into a fixed-size working memory, and after about 30 minutes the agent has to compress or start over.
board.eg: You ask your agent to run a 600-line test suite. The raw output is 56 KB - and now a quarter of the agent's memory is gone on one result.

board.say: You install Context Mode once - it runs as a background service (an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, a bridge that gives AI agents extra tools) and starts intercepting tool results automatically.
board.eg: One command in your terminal, or install from the Claude Code plugin marketplace. It activates automatically for every session.

board.say: The raw output from tools your agent uses: test results, log files, search results, file contents - anything the agent would normally read in full.
board.eg: A Playwright browser snapshot (56 KB), 20 GitHub issues (59 KB), or a server access log (45 KB).

board.say: It intercepts tool output before the agent sees it, runs it in an isolated process, and hands back only a small summary.
steps: Runs each tool's output in a sandboxed process so the raw data never enters the conversation - only the printed result does
Indexes the full output in a local database so the agent can search it later by keyword if it needs more detail
Tracks file edits, decisions, and task progress in a session log that survives compression, so the agent remembers what happened
board.eg: 47 file reads totaling 700 KB become one sandboxed call returning 3.6 KB - the agent gets what it needs without filling its memory.

board.say: Longer, cheaper AI coding sessions with less wasted memory.

outputs.eg: A session that used to compress at 30 minutes runs for about 3 hours before needing to compress
A long Claude Code session on Opus 5.5 dropped from $7.20 to $2.49 in the project's paired tests (155 of 168 runs cost less)
After compression, a 2 KB snapshot restores the agent's awareness of what happened earlier in the session

before: Your AI coding agent fills its working memory after about 30 minutes of real work. It has to compress or start over, losing track of what it was doing.
Every tool result enters the conversation at full size - a 56 KB test snapshot, a 59 KB batch of issues - even if the agent only needed a one-line answer from each.
after: Tool results are processed in the background and only summaries enter the conversation. A 315 KB session becomes 5.4 KB, and the full data is still searchable.
Sessions run for hours instead of minutes, and the agent picks up where it left off after compression because its decisions and progress are saved locally.
uses_note: Context Mode is 235 days old. The project claims adoption at large companies, but an independent review found those claims come from a self-authored tracking file, not confirmed case studies. No named real-world adopters could be verified.

footprint.disk: Installed via npm (`npx -y context-mode`). Package size not published. Session data stored in SQLite databases under `~/.context-mode/content/`.
footprint.memory: No data found. Runs tool output in subprocesses; supports 12 language sandboxes (JavaScript, Python, Shell, Go, Rust, and more).
footprint.runs_on: Mac, Windows, and Linux. Requires Node.js 22.5+ (or Bun). Windows has known issues (see Watch). Linux needs glibc 2.31+ for the native SQLite module, or a C++20 compiler to build from source.

source.title: Context Mode README: installation and requirements

best_for: You run long AI coding sessions and hit context limits regularly - especially sessions over 30 minutes that compress and lose track of earlier work
You want to reduce your AI coding costs without changing how you work - install once and the savings happen automatically
skip_if: You mostly run short sessions that finish in a few minutes - the overhead of indexing and sandboxing adds no value for quick tasks
You need a fully open-source tool - Context Mode changed from MIT to the Elastic License 2.0, which is source-available but not open-source, and cannot be offered as a hosted service
You work on Windows - an open issue reports a batch execution call that ran for over four hours without completing

alternatives.name: Curated tool lists
alternatives.line: Reduce context by loading fewer tools. Context Mode handles output size; this handles input size. They work together.

alternatives.line: The free local plugin with sandbox and index. The paid Context Mode gateway ($49/month) adds cost controls, team policies, and analytics.

watch: **License changed from MIT to Elastic License 2.0.** ELv2 is source-available, not open-source. You can use and modify it freely, but you cannot offer it as a hosted service to others.

**The 98% claim measures bytes saved, not answer quality.** The developer says 'We haven't run formal benchmarks on answer quality yet.' Fewer bytes in context could mean the agent misses details. An independent reviewer recommends checking your own numbers with `/context-mode:ctx-stats`.

**Windows support has known issues.** A GitHub issue (#947) reports a batch execution call that stayed in flight for over four hours. The reviewer advises Windows users to check the issue tracker first.

**Adoption claims are self-reported.** The README shows badges for Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon, and others, but an independent review found these come from the project's own tracking file and could not be confirmed.
